questions.question: Give a short account of Leonardo da Vinci's life.
questions.expected_answer: Leonardo was born in 1452 in or near Vinci, in Tuscany, near Florence, in Italy. As a teenager he became an apprentice to the artist Andrea del Verrocchio in Florence. He worked for powerful patrons in Milan, Florence and Rome, and at the end of his life moved to France at the invitation of the King of France, where he died in 1519.

questions.question: Describe Leonardo's contribution as an artist.
questions.expected_answer: He used Renaissance techniques such as perspective and soft blending of light and shadow to make paintings look real. His most famous painting is the Mona Lisa, now in the Louvre in Paris. He painted The Last Supper on a wall in Milan and made thousands of drawings, including the Vitruvian Man.

questions.question: Explain why Leonardo is seen as a scientist and inventor as well as an artist.
questions.expected_answer: He filled thousands of notebook pages, often in mirror writing, with careful studies of the human body, such as muscles, bones and the heart, and of nature, such as how birds fly and water flows. He designed flying machines, a parachute, an armoured vehicle, diving equipment and bridges. Most were never built, but they show his curiosity and his habit of observing and testing ideas.
